relationships.description: The interaction recipe is paired with a reusable state machine whose flow (e.g. loading/success/error) it typically drives or accompanies, so the two are reused together wherever that interaction recurs.
relationships.evidence: The action pattern's definition file or design-system documentation names the state pattern it is designed to work with, or both are co-referenced by the same set of components in the UX spec.

relationships.description: The action pattern prescribes the input modality and feedback sequence that a button, link, menu entry or voice command must follow when activated, making the control a conforming instance of the recipe.
relationships.evidence: The action component's spec or code declares a pattern reference (e.g. pattern: 'confirm-then-toast') and its click handler emits exactly the feedback steps the pattern defines.

relationships.description: The action pattern dictates how a lifecycle-bound side effect such as submit or navigate must behave and what feedback it produces, so state actions executing that interaction comply with the recipe's prescribed sequence.
relationships.evidence: The state action's definition references the action pattern id, and its on-enter/on-transition handler produces the toast, modal or route change listed in that pattern's feedback sequence.

relationships.description: Completing the interaction recipe emits the named UI event that fires a state transition, moving the experience from one state to the next as part of the pattern's feedback sequence.
relationships.evidence: The action pattern's feedback or outcome step dispatches an event name that matches the trigger event declared on the state transition in the state machine definition.

relationships.description: The action pattern relies on a shared motion definition to animate the UI changes in its feedback sequence, such as a modal appearing or a route change, rather than defining its own animation.
relationships.evidence: The action pattern spec references the transition template id for one of its feedback steps, and the rendered animation uses that template's type, duration and easing tokens.

notes: Governing both ActionComponent and StateAction blurs the pattern's scope: it is described as applied to action components, whereas StateActions are automatic lifecycle effects. Also, triggering a StateTransition directly from a reusable pattern is odd; instance-level ActionComponents usually emit the triggering event, so 'triggers' may belong on ActionComponent instead.
